title: The Path of a Step: A Swing That Starts and Ends Slowly, Clears the Ground, and Asks the Servos for Less Than They Have

artifact.note: the path of a foot through one step: the swing from the place the foot leaves to the place it lands, along the ground by a smooth rise from rest to rest (minimum jerk) and in height by a curve that is zero with its first two derivatives at both ends and has its top at the step's height; the stance as a straight line back at the body's speed; the peak speed and acceleration of the swing; how high the foot is over an obstacle in the way; and the greatest joint rate the swing needs along the whole path (by the inverse kinematics at points of the path), to be set against what the servos can do
